title: Umbra bridge handoff notes - 2028-02-14
body:
Shift window: 2028-02-13 23:00 UTC -> 2028-02-14 07:00 UTC
Owner on duty: Ava Martinez (primary), Noah Kim (secondary)

High-level summary:
- Brief P1-like latency surge (p95 and p99) in hosted inference routes between 00:18-00:35 UTC. Impact: elevated tail latency for ~3 high-throughput customers (no error-rate increase, but customer-visible timeouts for one waveform streaming client).
- Trigger: sudden KV-cache eviction storm on a subset of Dedicated pools after a canary model rollout (redwood-open/psi-7b-8q -> new attention kernel changed sequence-length batching behavior).
- Automated fallback to smaller compatible variant (psi-7b-4q) for affected requests executed successfully at 00:24 UTC; latency reduced but remained ~30% above baseline until 00:35 UTC when cache stabilised.
- No data loss or SLA breach escalation opened; post-shift follow-up recommended to avoid recurrence.

Incident timeline (short):
- 00:17 UTC: Pager alert for p95 > 2.5s on /v1/generate (hosted-us-west-2).
- 00:18 UTC: Observed increased cache_miss_rate on pool dedicated-us-west-2-a (cache eviction spikes in metrics: kv_evictions_per_min +420%).
- 00:20 UTC: Correlate with MR!211 canary rollout logs — new kernel scheduling flagged for longer warmup.
- 00:22 UTC: Manually applied temporary rate-limit bump to routing policy for affected customers to reduce queue pressure (route: customer-high-throttle -> reduced concurrency to 60%).
- 00:24 UTC: Automated model fallback engaged for failing route; traffic moved to psi-7b-4q variant.
- 00:30 UTC: Cache hit-rate recovered to within 90% of baseline; p95 trending down.
- 00:35 UTC: All key metrics back to normal; alert auto-resolved.

Mitigations performed during shift:
- Enabled fallback policy earlier in routing config for the canary group (command used: infractl route update --name hosted-canary --fallback-model redwood-open/psi-7b-4q --concurrency 60).
- Scaled dedicated-us-west-2-a pool +1 instance to relieve short-term pressure (autoscaling override).
- Applied temporary increase to per-tenant queue timeouts for waveform streaming clients to prevent client-side timeouts while internal tail latency resolved.

Immediate follow-ups (owners & due dates):
- Priya Singh: Reproduce eviction storm in staging using sequence-length distribution from affected customers. Due: 2028-02-16. Linked: JIRA-SITE-9772.
- Noah Kim: Patch runbook RB-042 (KV cache eviction) with new diagnostic commands and safe rollback steps. Due: 2028-02-15.
- Ava Martinez: Schedule postmortem meeting with runtime and model-onboarding teams; invite owners of MR!211. Due: 2028-02-15 15:00 UTC.
- Oncall rotation: Add temporary watch on dedicated-us-west-2-a for next 48 hours (priority: 24/7 lightweight sampling). Owner: next shift.

Runbook deltas recommended:
- RB-042: Add section "Detecting kernel-induced eviction storms" with the following checks:
  * metrics to query: kv_evictions_per_min, kv_cache_hit_rate, runtime_queue_depth, model_variant_latency_by_seq_len
  * diagnostics commands:
    - curl -s ${OBS_API}/query?metric=kv_evictions_per_min
    - infractl pool tail --pool dedicated-us-west-2-a --lines 200 | grep eviction
  * safe mitigation steps: increase pool capacity, enable model fallback, reduce canary concurrency to 5%
- RB-042: Add post-incident checklist entry to mark the model rollout as restricted until cache padding is validated in staging.

Open items / risks for next shift:
- MR!211 still in canary for non-critical traffic (partial rollout). If rollout resumes without cache-padding changes, we risk repeat.
- One customer (acct-c-9012) reported intermittent user timeouts during 00:20-00:30 UTC. Customer Success ticket opened: CS-3249. CS will coordinate any required credits after postmortem.
- Observability: need a synthetic that reproduces long-sequence behavior causing evictions; product/solutions engineering should own a dedicated synthetic within 2 weeks.

Operational notes & quick commands (for next on-call):
- Quick check for same issue:
  * OBS query: "sum(rate(kv_evictions_per_min[5m])) by (pool)"
  * Check model fallback state: infractl route get --name hosted-canary | jq .fallback_status
  * Force safe fallback (if appropriate): infractl route update --name hosted-canary --force-fallback true
- To temporarily protect cache: infractl pool update dedicated-us-west-2-a --cache-padding 0.25 (note: padding > 0.2 can increase memory pressure; confirm with runtime team)

Customer-facing notes (if asked):
- Short blurb for CS: "We observed a transient spike in inference tail latency tied to a kernel scheduling change in a canary model rollout. We activated our automated fallback and scaled capacity; latency returned to normal within ~20 minutes. We'll follow up with a postmortem and preventative changes."

Next shift checklist (what to look at first):
1) Verify dedicated-us-west-2-a pool metrics for kv_evictions_per_min and cache hit rate (top-of-shift snapshot).
2) Confirm MR!211 canary status and current canary concurrency.
3) Watch CS-3249 for customer impact updates.
4) If eviction rate > 200% baseline, escalate to runtime lead and trigger the runbook RB-042 mitigation steps.

Notes to PMs / runtime team:
- Request: hold further canary progress for MR!211 until Priya reproduces eviction pattern in staging and we validate cache-padding configuration.
- Consider a small experiment to add sequence-length-aware pre-batching to avoid sudden eviction waves when long-sequence traffic enters a small pool.

Attachments & references (links included above):
- Postmortem placeholder: CONFLUENCE-SEQ-4821 (create detailed timeline + graphs)
- Jira: JIRA-SITE-9772 (investigate eviction storm)
- MR: https://gitlab.com/redwood/runtime/merge_requests/211

Shift sign-off:
- Signed out at 07:05 UTC. Next oncall: Liam O'Connor (starts 07:00 UTC) — handoff confirmed on Slack (#sre-bridge).
- If any escalations occur, ping oncall-mobile and call runtime-lead (ringdown: runtime-lead -> eng-vp).

End of notes.
